h: פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר א׳ Parshas Parah — Maamar Aleph

p: "This is the statute of the Torah
אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ לֵאמֹר וְגוֹמֵר [בַּמִּדְבַּר יט, ב].
"This is the statute of the parah,"
כְּדִכְתִיב זֹאת חֻקַּת הַפֶּסַח [שְׁמוֹת יב, מג].
as it is written, "This is the statute of the Pesach" (Shemos 12:43).
But in the Pesikta Rabbasi it appears
of the Piska of Parah, parsha 14):
just as the Torah is expounded
And this needs to be understood:
and every word of the words of Torah!
So why should Parshas Parah differ
from all the parshiyos of the Torah,
and why did it need to say
"and this parsha too," and so on,
"so too this one," and so on?
is the matter of what they said,
that it is equal to the whole Torah.
that for this reason it is written
"This is the statute of the Torah":
that through the reading of this parsha
so that all the words of Torah are engraved,
from all the impurities of the yetzer hara.
which is equal to the whole Torah,
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
עַל שְׁמִירַת יוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
for the keeping of one day of Shabbos,
And so it is written in the holy Zohar
as they said in the Mechilta
"There He set for him a statute" —
That is, through the mitzvah of Shabbos
there are engraved in the heart
And so Parshas Parah is called chok,
and this is the reason it is said,
"This is the statute of the Torah."
And it is said in this parsha specifically
And this is what they said in the holy Zohar
It should have said chok haTorah;
a dalet and nun joined together, and so on.
which is the fifty gates of understanding;
as has been explained many times.
And the essence of the Torah
drag him to the beis midrash;
and the beis midrash is the place
of the novel insights in halachos
And the verse has taught us
that through the reading of Parshas Parah
the words of Torah are engraved in the heart,
and it helps to repair the "much anger,"
And this is what they said in the Yerushalmi
(מְגִילָּה פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ה כה, ב
for on the first of Nissan the Mishkan was erected,
and on the second the parah was burned;
so why does Parah come first?
Because it is the purification of all Yisrael.
And it needs to be understood
why the reading of the parsha is called
why did they institute the reading of the parsha?
If it is to caution Yisrael
to offer their Pesach offerings in purity
And if the Beis HaMikdash is rebuilt,
then the ashes of the parah will be revealed;
so that they offer their Pesach offerings in purity?
And if so, at any rate,
they should have put Parshas HaChodesh first;
so why did they put Parshas Parah first?
But the matter is as we have said,
that the reading of the parsha helps
from the impurities of the yetzer hara,
And this is what they said in the Yerushalmi:
that it is the purification of all Yisrael —
that the reading of Parshas Parah
from the impurity of the yetzer hara.
And because the matter of the parah helps
to repair the root of the yetzer hara,
and its root is from the serpent,
who brought ruin into the world.
And therefore the sprinkling of the parah helps
to purify from the impurity of a corpse,
for this the serpent brought into the world.
And this is the matter of what they said
he found the Holy One, blessed be He,
occupied, with His book in His hand,
in the parsha of the red heifer:
"This is the statute of the Torah."
The Holy One, blessed be He, said:
From where do we know this?
פִּי צַדִּיק יֶהְגֶּה חָכְמָה וְגוֹמֵר [תְּהִלִּים לז, ל]
"The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom," etc. (Tehillim 37:30).
The mouth of the Righteous One of the world
In "This is the statute of the Torah."
And afterward it is stated in the Pesikta
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and saying a halachah in the name of its author:
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר וְכוּלֵּי [פָּרָה פֶּרֶק א מִשְׁנָה א]
(וְכֵן הוּא בְּבַמִּדְבַּר רַבָּה חֻקַּת יט, ז
(and so it is in Bamidbar Rabbah, Chukas 19:7,
of the laws of the red heifer,
which is the essence of Yisrael's purification —
Therefore it was precise at first
and wrote, "with His book in His hand" —
And afterward it used the wording,
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
with Parshas Parah," and so on —
the laws of the red heifer,
which is the Mishnah at the beginning of Parah.
And as for its saying "the voice
of the Holy One, blessed be He" —
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ג, א)
The voice comes to speech, and so on;
"The word of Hashem" — this is halachah;
and it is the seventh day,
which is the life-force of the speech
And this is what they said in the Pesikta,
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
with the parsha of Parah, and so on:
a calf in its first year," and so on.
This is the life-force of speech,
the speech in the heart of the Sages,
along the lines of what is said (Yeshayahu 59:21),
"My words which I have placed in your mouth."
And this is the essence of Torah she'b'al peh,
therefore it was precise and wrote,
"with His book in His hand," and so on.
to the Shabbos on which Parshas Parah is read,
for it is a parsha written
while the obligation to read it
is from an enactment of the Sages,
who instituted reading it on this Shabbos —
and this is the power of Torah she'b'al peh.
as they said in the holy Zohar
and even the mitzvos and enactments of the Elders
And this is what they said:
"The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom" —
the mouth of the Righteous One of the world
In "This is the statute of the Torah" —
And this is what they said: "And why?
The Holy One, blessed be He, said:
that is, the reading of the parsha
from the impurity of the yetzer hara;
and this is the power of all the words of Torah together
And for this reason it is written,
"This is the statute of the Torah,"
and not "the statute of the parah."
does He read in the parsha of the red heifer
"This is the statute of the Torah"?
The Holy One, blessed be He, said:
for it is equal to the whole Torah

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 1 — “Shabbos is also called chok, ‘chok — this is Shabbos’: on Shabbos one merits Torah she'b'al peh, engraved in the heart without toil.” Rav Tzadok there adds the mechanism: what weekday toil achieves, Shabbos engraves in rest, and so it guards against the yetzer hara’s anger. This is why Parshas Parah, a chok like Shabbos, can work the same engraving.

That is why the verse says “statute of the Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 180b (Chukat) — “‘This is the statute of the Torah’—it should have said ‘the law of the Torah’; what is ‘statute’? We have explained that heh was dalet, but tav is dalet and nun joined as one. Why is nun called by this name? As it says, ‘You shall not deceive one another’: now she has a shining face and deceives people; afterward she strikes like a serpent, destroys and kills, and says, ‘I have done no wrong.’ ... Tav is all joined together: dalet, nun.” The Zohar develops the letters of chukat through dalet, nun and tav, and then expounds nun in connection with deception and the serpent. Rav Tzadok reads that conjunction through the fifty gates of understanding and the Oral Torah. The wordplay should not be reduced to a literal rule of Hebrew spelling.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 3 — “The second Luchos included all of Torah she'b'al peh… this was needed after the corruption, the ‘much wisdom’ to repair the ‘much anger,’ as Nedarim 22b says.” This supplies the Gemara behind Rav Tzadok’s formula. Had Yisrael not sinned, only the five books would have been given. The Oral Torah was given as the answer to the anger of the yetzer.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 7 — “Now that we have no ashes of the parah, ‘let our lips pay for bulls’ (Hoshea 14:3) through reading the parashah, which works to bring this into the heart little by little.” Here Rav Tzadok answers the same question about our time. The reading itself does the purifying that the ashes once did, and it comes before Pesach on purpose.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbati 14 — “Rabbi Acha said in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Chanina: When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied with His book in His hand, engaged in reading this passage, the passage of the red heifer: ‘This is the statute of the Torah.’ Why? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘I am engaged only in the purification of Israel.’ Whence? ‘The mouth of the righteous meditates wisdom, and his tongue speaks judgment’: the mouth of the Righteous One of the world meditates wisdom, occupying Himself with Torah. With which Torah? ‘This is the statute of the Torah.’”

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:7 — “Rabbi Acha said in the name of Rabbi Chanina: When Moses ascended on high, he heard the voice of the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and studying the passage of the red heifer, stating a law in the name of its author: ‘Rabbi Eliezer says: A calf is in its first year, and a cow in its second.’ He said before Him: ‘Master of the worlds, may it be Your will that he come from my descendants.’ He said to him: ‘By your life, he comes from your descendants,’ as it is written, ‘The name of the one was Eliezer’—the name of that distinguished one.” The parallel is also transmitted in Tanchuma, Chukat 8. Rav Tzadok distinguishes the book held in the first account from the spoken teaching bearing the name of a future Sage in this account.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Parah 1:1 — “Rabbi Eliezer says: A calf is in its first year, and a cow in its second. The Sages say: A calf is in its second year, and a cow in its third or fourth. Rabbi Meir says: Even one five years old. An old cow is valid, but we do not wait for it, lest it blacken and become invalid.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik 221:1 — “Voice is general and speech is particular, as the Zohar says at the beginning of Shemot. Therefore the Written Torah is called ‘voice,’ and the Oral Torah ‘speech.’ Likewise, what is made heard in the heart is only general: to know His divinity and seek Him.... Through the understanding in a person’s heart it becomes particular in every detail, according to what he needs.... ‘With a voice’ means God’s will for that day in general, for the angels know no more: the Oral Torah is below, in the hands of the Sages of Israel, and the particulars are clarified by human beings on that day.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The maamar distinguishes the divine voice that gives life from the specific halakhah spoken by a Sage. This parallel explains the distinction’s human side: the general divine call becomes particular Torah through the understanding and daily work of Israel’s Sages.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, vol. I, Bo — “The statute of the Pesach corresponds to ‘I am Hashem,’ which includes all positive mitzvos; the statute of the parah, to ‘You shall have no other gods,’ which includes all negative mitzvos.” The Izhbitzer also starts from the contrast with “the statute of the Pesach.” For him too the parah is not one rite. It is the cleansing of the heart from evil that underlies the whole Torah.
